text:
maria (support): Folks, getting a customer escalation — p99 latency for /v1/generate jumped ~3x since ~09:12 UTC for tenant acme-inc. They hit 850ms p99 on tiny prompts (<=16 tokens). No auth/billing errors, just latency. Suspect continuous-batcher config change rolled yesterday.

devon (eng-runtime): Ack. Which model/route? Any config diff?

maria (support): model: redwood-fft-7b, route: /generate-chat, region: us-west-2. Customer notes they did nothing on their side. I dug into tenant overrides — we toggled `batching.grace_window_ms` from 5 -> 25 for the host pool yesterday as part of a burst mitigation rollout.

alex (eng-sre): That matches classic hold-time vs tail tradeoff. Small prompts suffer when grace window is high -> tiny requests wait longer behind slow-growing batches. Can you paste p95/p99 numbers from the last 6 hours?

maria (support): From datadog (last 6h): p50 40ms, p95 120ms, p99 850ms. Prior to rollout (24h earlier) p99 was ~200ms.

devon (eng-runtime): OK. I'll pull batcher traces for the pool. Meanwhile can we repro locally with tiny prompt workload? Use this quick script:

```bash
# repro tiny-prompt burst
for i in {1..1000}; do \
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY\" -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-fft-7b\",\"input\":\"hi\"}' &\
  if (( i % 200 == 0 )); then wait; fi
done
```

alex (eng-sre): I checked traces — many requests show `batch_wait_ms` ~24-25ms before batch flush, and single-request batches for tiny prompts are queuing behind long-running requests. CPU and GPU utilization normal. This is config-induced.

sre-oncall (bot): New alert: pool us-west-2-host-7b p99 latency > 700ms (alerting at 09:15 UTC).

devon (eng-runtime): Minimally invasive mitigation: reduce `batching.grace_window_ms` to 6ms for the affected host pool and tenant routing policy. That should lower single-request queuing and collapse p99. Tradeoff: will increase throughput overhead and cost slightly.

maria (support): Customer ok with temporary mitigation. Please canary for 10% of hosts then expand.

alex (eng-sre): I'll prepare canary config change. Plan: 1) change grace_window_ms 25 -> 6 on 2 hosts (canary) 2) monitor p99 + batch size distribution for 15m 3) if good, roll to remaining hosts. Rolling out now. (reacted with :rocket:)

deploy-bot: Starting config canary: pool=us-west-2-host-7b, targets=2 hosts, config_change={"batching.grace_window_ms":6}. Canary id=canary-20260317-01

devon (eng-runtime): Adding quick dashboard: `batch.wait_ms`, `batch.size.histogram`, `request.p99` and `cost.tokens_per_request`. Also logging per-tenant small_prompt_rate to ensure we don't regress hot tenants.

alex (eng-sre): Canary results after 10m: canary hosts p99 dropped from ~820ms -> 170ms. Batch size histogram shows median batch size from 1.1 -> 1.05 (tiny change), but tail flush reduced. No CPU/GPU pressure increase observed.

deploy-bot: Canary succeeded. Rolling config to remaining hosts with 30s stagger. Roll id=roll-20260317-02

maria (support): Customer confirmed latency improved to acceptable levels. They reported p99 ~180ms within 8 minutes. Thanks.

devon (eng-runtime): For follow-up: need smarter heuristics — dynamic grace window based on input length distribution and detected small_prompt_rate. Also consider fast-path for single-token prompts: immediate flush if batch size==1 for <32-token requests. Filing ticket.

alex (eng-sre): Opened ticket SRE-4821: "adaptive-batcher: dynamic grace_window + single-prompt fastpath" with repro steps + canary results + dashboards.

maria (support): Marking escalation resolved from support side. Will keep customer on watch.

devon (eng-runtime): Repro note for engineers: run the curl loop above with `-c 200` concurrency and compare `batch.wait_ms` traces. If you want a tighter repro, use small prompt bursts interleaved with 500ms long completions to force queuing.

alex (eng-sre): Final: added a temp knob in runtime to override tenant grace_window to 6ms for tiny-prompt-heavy tenants. Schedule roadmap item to implement the adaptive heuristic. Closing thread in 24h if no regressions. :white_check_mark:
